nodes.prompt:
Implement the change described in the current issue/branch. Keep the diff
focused. Choose a commit granularity that fits the work — one commit per
refactoring unit for refactors, per file for sweeps, per feature slice
for new code — and state your choice in the first commit message. Commit
as you go: a node timeout must never lose finished work. End every commit
message with the trailer `Co-Authored-By: oh-my-graph <graphs@oh-my-graph.dev>`
(the attribution convention in CONTRIBUTING.md). When done, reply
with a one-line summary of what you changed.

Continue the work — or, on a retried attempt, start from the branch's
committed state — and run the end-to-end checks (make local). If the
diff touches concurrency-sensitive code, also stress its tests (e.g.
`go test <affected packages> -race -count=300`, or your stack's
equivalent) — a flaky test passes a single run, and determinism is
the claim under test.
Run every check SYNCHRONOUSLY and wait for it to finish — never in the
background. Your FINAL reply is the verdict: never end the turn on an
interim report. Report exactly PASS if everything succeeds, or FAIL
with the failing step.

Review the current diff for security issues (injection, secrets, unsafe
shell, unsafe exec, authz gaps). The e2e verdict was: {{ artifacts.e2e | inline }}.
Reply with a short bulleted list of findings, or "no security issues found".

Review the current diff for style, naming, and simplicity.

If the diff adds or edits test doubles or concurrency tests, also verify:
every synchronization field is actually wired (no dead channels, no
wall-clock fallback arms) and no assertion is satisfiable by a record or
node simply being absent.
Reply with a short bulleted list, or "no style issues found".
